caseno: Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 506 of 1994
lawyer:
Mr. Muhammad Korban Ali, Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
For the Respondents: Not represented
parties:
Abu Taher and others ----- Petitioners
Vs
Sharifa Begum and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
A.T.M. Afzal, J: Plaintiff-petitioners filed Title Suit No. 4 of 1984 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla for a declaration that they are the exclusive owners of the suit land by way of inheritance. The Suit property Consists 21 plots comprising an area of 6 kanis 1-3/2 gandas of land. Their case is that the C S recorded tenants of the Suit land Kala Gazi and others defaulted in payment of rent and the landlord instituted rent suit No. 8655 of 1912 and got a decree In execution of the said decree the suit land was sold in auction on 16.5.1934 and the predecessors of the plaintiffs Abdul Wahab, Abdur Rahman and Abdus Samad purchased the suit jote. The sale was confirmed on 16.6.1934. The auction purchasers got possession of the suit land after evicting the ex-tenants. After eviction the defendants predecessors asked the auction purchasers to give them shelter whereupon they were given permission to reside there after erecting huts thereon. The auction purchasers amicably participated the entire suit land each of them getting 1/3rd share. They had been possessing their respective shares and their names were recorded in S A Khatian But recently it was found that S A Khatian No. 9 was illegally prepared in the name of the defendants predecessors in collusion with the Government officials although they have no right, title and possession in respect of the suit land In order to remove the cloud upon their title because of such illegal recording by the defendants predecessors, the plaintiffs instituted the suit. 

 2. Defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing a written statement The Defendants admitted that Kala Gazi and others are the C.S. record owners of the suit property. They, however, allege that one of the co-sharer of the jote Jafor Ali who was the owner of 1/3rd share of the suit jote sold 4 plot, Nos. 431, 435, 443 and 436/459 to the predecessors of the plaintiffs and they are in possession of the said 4 plots. Karim Ali another co-sharer of the jote died leaving behind only daughter Bali Bibi who inherited the share of her father. Although Jafor Ali sold his entire share to Ganu Mia and predecessors of the plaintiffs he did not execute any kabala in their favour Ganu Mia and the predecessors of the plaintiffs in order to avoid future complications decided to put the jote-into auction sale by keeping rent in arrear and to purchase the same by the money of Ganu Miah in the benami of the predecessors of the plaintiffs who were already previous purchasers from Jafor Ali. Thereafter the suit jote was sold in auction in rent Execution Case No. 4417 of 1933 and the jote was auction purchased by Ganu Mia in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs as arranged. After the rent sale Ganu Mia and Bali Bibi continued to possess their share as before and the plaintiffs predecessors continued to possess their purchased land as before. No delivery of possession was made through Court or otherwise after the suit property was sold in auction. The predecessors of the defendants were never evicted from suit homestead or other lands. S.A. Khatian has been correctly prepared in the name of the defendants predecessors. 

 6. Mr. Muhammad Korban Ali learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the learned Judge of the High Court Division failed to consider that the learned Additional District Judge upon reference to the rent suit filed by the landlord and the consequent rent execution case supported among other documents by the certified copy of the rent suit register (filed in the lower appellate Court) correctly found title of the plaintiffs to the entire suit land. He also submits that both the Courts below found that the plaintiffs filed a series of rent receipts showing payment of rent for the entire suit land since long and the S.A. Khatian was prepared in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs. Mr. Korban Ali has argued that the well-considered judgment of the lower Appeal late Court has been wrongly set aside in revision.
